metadata.sampling_method: Per platform x length bucket, select the lexicographically smallest SHA-256 digests of platform + normalized content; duplicate normalized content is excluded. A separate full row-key SHA-256 chooses canonical metadata deterministically.

population.unique_count_method: cardinality of SHA-256 digests of normalized content; collision risk is negligible

interpretation.summary: C is the closest category because sampled 1~20 character reviews broadly saturate at >=90. However, the 41+ group saturates at least as strongly. Across this unlabeled new-data sample, P_text outputs concentrate globally in the NORMAL direction, mostly around scores 94~96; this does not support a short-specific effect and does not establish ground-truth generalization failure.
interpretation.decision_aid: Diagnostic heuristic: C when every 1~20 bucket has >=70% scores >=90; B when either 1~5 or 6~10 does; otherwise A. This is not a policy threshold.
limitations: Sampled inference, not inference over all raw rows.
The new real-world sample is unlabeled; this is not a ground-truth performance evaluation, and no Accuracy, Recall, or FPR is estimated.
NORMAL output concentration does not establish model generalization failure or prove that suspicious reviews cannot be detected.
Short reviews are not assumed to be fake or suspicious.
Writing style may differ by platform.
Unique-content sampling differs from actual traffic weighting.
Weak suspicious evidence is not equivalent to sufficient trustworthy evidence.
A separate positive-control inference has not yet been run.
